requirement:
A result of the `habeas` line-range form, `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`,
`ast_grep`, or `references` whose serialized JSON exceeds 32 KiB MUST be
returned in pages. Each page MUST hold whole entries of the result's arrays, such
as inputs, matches, nodes, or sites, with its accompanying definitions, in the
result's order, and MUST NOT exceed 32 KiB unless a single entry does, which
then forms a page of its own. Every paged result MUST include:

```text
page: {
    total_entries: Integer,
    returned_entries: Integer,
    next: String?,
}
```

`next` MUST be an opaque token when entries remain and null on the last page. The
harness MUST expose a `next_page({ token: String })` tool returning the following
page of the same result, in the same shape. Pages MUST be kept only until the
assessment that requested them finishes; an unknown token, including one from
another assessment, MUST return an explanatory tool error. A result within the
limit MUST be returned whole, without `page`. Only inputs on pages delivered to
the model MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`.
rationale:
I found no gap. The code carries out every obligation in `requirements.authoring.result_pages`, and each obligation has a test.

**Reachability.** `converse` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`) carries the {impl}. It creates one `pages::ResultPages` per conversation and passes it to `tools::dispatch_paged`. From there the paging code is reachable: `ResultPages::deliver`, `paginate`, `page_definitions`, `render`, `token`, and `next_page`. The `search`, `structural`, `references`, `outline`, `list_files`, and `read` functions that build the results are reached the same way. The {impl} markers on `PAGE_LIMIT`, `TOKEN_LENGTH`, and `REFERENCE_ARRAYS` also cover the constants those functions use.

**Obligations, code and tests**
- **Results over 32 KiB are paged, and smaller ones are returned whole without `page`.** `deliver` renders the whole result and compares `to_string().len()` with `PAGE_LIMIT` (32 × 1024). At or below the limit it returns the result unchanged. The test `an_entry_exceeding_the_limit_forms_a_page_of_its_own_and_small_results_stay_whole` asserts there is no `page` key on small `habeas` and `list_files` results.
- **The tools covered are the `habeas` line-range form, `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`, `ast_grep`, and `references`.** `dispatch_paged` sends all of them through `pages.deliver`.
  - The line-range form returns `Listing::inputs`.
  - `outline` and `list_files` return `Listing::array`.
  - `search`, `structural`, and `declared_query` return `Listing::object(&["matches"], …)`.
  - `references` returns `Listing::object(REFERENCE_ARRAYS, …)`.
  - The `item`, `requirements`, and `definition` forms of `habeas` and the `github` tool are not paged, which matches the text.
  - Tests cover `list_files`, `outline`, the `habeas` line-range form, and `references`. `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` have no paging test of their own. They use the same generic `Listing::object` and `deliver` path as the tested `references`, with no extra conditional logic, so I don't count that as a gap.
- **Each page holds whole entries of the result's arrays, with their accompanying definitions, in the result's order.** `paginate` builds consecutive ranges of whole entries. `render` places each entry back in its own array by index, and `page_definitions` supplies the definitions for a page's entries. `large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order` checks listings and outlines for order, no repeats, and pages filled before the next starts. `paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs` checks inputs and definitions. `reference_results_page_definitions_then_sites` checks that definitions come before sites.
- **A page does not exceed 32 KiB unless a single entry does, and that entry forms its own page.** `paginate` estimates sizes from above. It starts from an overhead that includes the longest `page` object and a 16-character token, and it counts every comma and every accompanying definition. An oversize entry is pushed as a page of its own. The tests assert `<= PAGE_LIMIT` on every page, and the big-function test asserts the single-entry oversize page.
- **Every paged result includes `page: {total_entries, returned_entries, next}`.** `deliver` builds this object, with `next` set to a token for every page except the last and null on the last. `all_pages` asserts the counts, and that `next` is null on the last page.
- **`next` is an opaque token.** `token()` returns random 16-character hex and avoids collisions with existing tokens.
- **The harness exposes `next_page({token})`, which returns the following page in the same shape.** `dispatch_paged` has a `next_page` arm. The tool definition in `definitions()` advertises it, and `next_page_is_advertised_and_paged_tools_explain_their_pages` checks the schema and the descriptions. Re-requesting a token returns the stored result, which the test compares with `delivered[1].result`.
- **Pages are kept only until the assessment finishes, and an unknown token returns an explanatory tool error.** `ResultPages` is a local in `converse` and is dropped when it returns. `next_page` returns an `unknown page token … valid only in the assessment …` error. The test checks both a fresh `ResultPages`, which stands in for another assessment, and the `next_page` tool with `"not-a-token"`.
- **Only inputs on pages delivered to the model are recorded under `delivered_inputs`.** Each page's `inputs` are exactly that page's entries plus its definitions. `converse` records only the `delivery.inputs` of tool calls it actually made, so undelivered pages are never recorded. `only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded` checks this end to end, and the pages test asserts per-page delivery.

No {fixme} references are involved.
